title: Mouse Blood Pressure Telemetry Procedure
author: Lin Zhong
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6xnhfme
materials: Mice are anesthetized with pentobarbital (50 mg/kg, IP).

steps.title: Prepare Surgical Site
steps.instruction: Shave and disinfect the ventral neck and upper dorsum of the mouse.

substeps.instruction: Apply Betadine to the area.
Apply 70% alcohol to the area.

steps.title: Create Ventral Incision
steps.instruction: Position the mouse supine on a heating pad and make a 1.5 cm midline incision through the skin underlying the trachea.

steps.title: Create Subcutaneous Tunnel
steps.instruction: Position the mouse in lateral decubitus and create a tunnel from the left ventral neck to the upper dorsum.

substeps.instruction: Advance a 3” 16G needle through the left ventral neck to the upper dorsum.

steps.title: Insert Transmitter Catheter
steps.instruction: Pass the catheter of a sterilized PA-C10 transmitter (DSI) through the needle tunnel.

substeps.instruction: Advance the catheter from the dorsal to the ventral side.
Carefully remove the needle, leaving the catheter in the ventral neck area and the transmitter body in the dorsal area.

steps.title: Isolate Carotid Artery
steps.instruction: Position the mouse supine again and locate and isolate the left carotid artery from surrounding tissue.

steps.title: Occlude Carotid Artery
steps.instruction: Use three pieces of non-absorbable 6-0 sutures to occlude the vessel.

substeps.instruction: Pass three 6-0 sutures under the carotid artery.
Position the cranial suture (furthest from the aorta) just below the bifurcation of the interior and exterior carotid arteries and tie a secure knot to permanently occlude the vessel.

steps.title: Insert Catheter into Artery
steps.instruction: Insert the catheter into the carotid artery using the remaining sutures.

substeps.instruction: Gently lift the suture closest to the aorta to temporarily occlude blood flow.
Make a small puncture in the carotid artery just distal to the middle suture.
Insert the catheter through the puncture and advance it towards the aorta until it reaches the occlusion sutures.
Loosely tie the middle suture to prevent catheter slippage and stop bleeding from the puncture.

steps.title: Position Catheter in Aortic Arch
steps.instruction: Advance the catheter tip into the aortic arch and secure it.

substeps.instruction: Release tension in the occlusion sutures.
Advance the catheter further beyond the suture towards the aorta until the tip is approximately 2 mm into the aortic arch.
Tie the occlusion suture and the middle suture to seal the vessel wall around the catheter and anchor it in place.

steps.title: Close Ventral Incision
steps.instruction: Close the skin incision using a 6-0 suture.

steps.title: Create Dorsal Pocket
steps.instruction: Create a subcutaneous dorsal pocket for the transmitter body.

substeps.instruction: Reposition the mouse prone.
Make a small incision starting from the needle puncture site.
Insert small surgical scissors into the incision and use blunt dissection to form the pocket.

steps.title: Implant Transmitter Body
steps.instruction: Place the transmitter body into the prepared dorsal pocket.

substeps.instruction: Irrigate the pocket with warm saline.
Insert the body of the transmitter into the pocket.

steps.title: Close Dorsal Incision
steps.instruction: Close the dorsal skin incision with a 6-0 suture.

steps.title: Post-Operative Care
steps.instruction: Provide recovery support and analgesia to the mouse.

substeps.instruction: Maintain the mouse on the heating pad until fully recovered from anesthesia.
Administer Buprenorphine SC immediately following surgery and every 8-12 hr for 72 hr.

steps.title: Verify Signal and Recovery
steps.instruction: Confirm transmitter functionality and allow for physiological recovery.

substeps.instruction: Upon recovery, place the mouse in its cage on a receiver platform (DSI) to confirm the fidelity of the blood pressure signal.
Allow mice to recover for 10 days after the surgical procedure before collecting blood pressure and heart rate data.
